items.title: Documentation Scope
items.text: This documentation tracks shipped behavior in the repository while preserving the long-term product vision.

items.title: Fast Path
items.text:
1. Read 02-quickstart.md.
  2. If you need custom transport, jump to 04-backends.md.
  3. If you need a queue sidecar, read 06-worker-engine.md.

items.title: What Fasthooks Is
items.text:
Fasthooks is a webhook framework for FastAPI applications that focuses on low-latency API responses and pluggable delivery architecture.

Core idea: 1. Your API route runs business logic. 2. Fasthooks captures event context. 3. Webhook delivery is offloaded through a backend path.

items.title: Design Principles
items.text:
• Keep core lightweight.
  • Ship only one backend by default: BackgroundTaskBackend.
  • Allow custom transports through BaseBackend.
  • Keep subscription storage abstract via BaseStore.

items.title: Components
items.text:
• Core decorator and event context.
  • Backend abstraction and default implementation.
  • Subscription stores.
  • Dispatcher for fan-out delivery with retries.
  • Optional sidecar engine for queue-style backends.

items.title: Mental Model
items.text: Use Fasthooks as a pipeline: - Emit phase in your API process. - Resolve subscribers from direct list or store. - Deliver to endpoints with signing/auth/retry behavior.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Python 3.9+
  • FastAPI app

items.title: Install
items.text: pip install fasthooks

items.title: Minimal Setup
items.text:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, FastAPI, Request

from fasthooks import Fasthooks
from fasthooks.backends import BackgroundTaskBackend

hooks = Fasthooks(
    backend=BackgroundTaskBackend(signing_secret="dev-secret")
)

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    async with hooks:
        yield

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

@app.post("/orders")
@hooks.hook("order.created")
async def create_order(request: Request, background_tasks: BackgroundTasks):
    return {"id": "ord_123", "status": "confirmed"}

items.title: Add Direct Subscribers
items.text:
from fasthooks.stores.base_store import WebhookSubscription

hooks = Fasthooks(
    backend=BackgroundTaskBackend(signing_secret="dev-secret"),
    subscribers={
        "order.created": [
            WebhookSubscription(
                event_name="order.created",
                target_url="https://example.com/webhooks/orders",
                auth_type="none",
            )
        ]
    },
)

items.title: Transform Payloads
items.text:
from fasthooks import FasthooksContext

def transform_order(ctx: FasthooksContext):
    return {
        "event": ctx.event_name,
        "owner": ctx.owner_id,
        "order_id": ctx.response_payload["id"],
    }

@app.post("/orders")
@hooks.hook("order.created", transform=transform_order)
async def create_order(request: Request, background_tasks: BackgroundTasks):
    return {"id": "ord_123", "status": "confirmed"}

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• BackgroundTaskBackend does not require a separate worker process.
  • Use the sidecar engine only for custom queue backends that implement consume and ack.

items.title: Fasthooks
items.text:
Main entry point that wires your backend, optional store, owner scope, and direct subscribers.

Constructor parameters: - backend: BaseBackend implementation. - store: optional store instance. - owner_id: optional global owner scope. - subscribers: optional event-to-subscriber map.

Lifecycle: - aclose() closes backend resources. - async context manager support is available via aenter/aexit.

items.title: hook Decorator
items.text:
hook(event_name, include_headers=False, include_request=False, include_response=True, transform=None, owner_id_resolver=None)

Behavior: 1. Calls original endpoint (sync or async). 2. Builds FasthooksContext. 3. Resolves payload through optional transform. 4. Publishes using backend.publish(...). 5. Uses FastAPI BackgroundTasks when provided.

Important details: - include_headers/include_request require request injection. - owner_id can come from constructor, endpoint kwargs, or owner_id_resolver. - If no BackgroundTasks instance is injected, emit path runs inline.

items.title: FasthooksContext
items.text:
Fields: - event_name - owner_id - timestamp - headers - request_payload - response_payload

Use it for deterministic payload shaping and metadata-aware transforms.

items.title: Error Surface
items.text:
• Missing request while include_headers/include_request is enabled raises RuntimeError.
  • Backend-specific delivery errors are handled by backend/dispatcher behavior.

items.title: Policy
items.text:
Fasthooks ships with one built-in backend: - BackgroundTaskBackend

Other transports should be implemented externally by subclassing BaseBackend.

items.title: BaseBackend Contract
items.text:
Methods expected: - publish(event_name, payload, owner_id, subscribers=None) - consume() - ack(event_id) - aclose()

Design intent: - publish is required for emit path. - consume and ack are for worker-driven queue backends. - aclose releases client/network resources.

items.title: BackgroundTaskBackend
items.text:
What it does: - Delivers to direct subscribers when provided. - Delivers via store-resolved subscriptions when store is configured. - Uses WebhookDispatcher for HTTP fan-out.

Features: - HMAC signing support. - Retry/backoff controls. - Dead-letter callback hook. - Async context manager and aclose support.

items.title: Custom Backend Template
items.text:
from typing import Any

from fasthooks.backends import BaseBackend
from fasthooks.stores.base_store import WebhookSubscription

class MyQueueBackend(BaseBackend):
    async def publish(
        self,
        event_name: str,
        payload: Any,
        owner_id: str | None,
        subscribers: list[WebhookSubscription] | None = None,
    ):
        ...

    async def consume(self):
        ...

    async def ack(self, event_id: str):
        ...

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        return None

items.title: Implementation Guidance
items.text:
• Keep signature parity with BaseBackend.
  • Do not mutate payload in transport layer unless documented.
  • Keep retry semantics in one place to avoid double retries.

items.title: BaseStore Contract
items.text:
Stores manage webhook subscriptions by event name.

Required methods: - add_subscription(...) - remove_subscription(subscription_id) - get_subscriptions(event_name) - update_subscription(subscription_id, ...)

Optional method: - get_subscription(subscription_id)

items.title: Included Stores
items.text:
• MemoryStore: in-memory implementation for development/testing.
  • SQLStore: SQLAlchemy async store for relational databases.

items.title: Subscription Model
items.text:
WebhookSubscription fields: - event_name - target_url - auth_type: bearer or none - auth_value - metadata

StoredWebhookSubscription adds: - id

items.title: Choosing a Store
items.text:
Use MemoryStore when: - local prototyping - short-lived process - test scenarios

Use SQLStore when: - durable subscriptions are needed - multiple instances share subscriptions - operational visibility is required

items.title: Custom Store Guidance
items.text:
• Keep event_name indexing efficient.
  • Use partial metadata merges for update paths.
  • Validate target_url and auth constraints near write boundaries.

items.title: Why It Exists
items.text:
The sidecar engine is for queue-backed custom backends that expose consume and ack behavior.

BackgroundTaskBackend does not use this loop.

items.title: FasthooksEngine Flow
items.text:
1. Consume event from backend.
  2. Dispatch to matching subscribers.
  3. Acknowledge via backend.ack(event.id).
  4. Continue processing even when one event fails.

items.title: CLI
items.text:
Entry point command: 

fasthooks start --backend-module myapp.backends:backend --store-module myapp.stores:store --signing-secret "secret"

Main options: - --backend-module module_path:instance - --store-module module_path:instance - --signing-secret value - --max-concurrency integer - --log-level level

items.title: Import Resolution Rules
items.text:
Module path format: - module.submodule:instance_name

Failure modes: - Invalid path format raises import error. - Missing module or attribute exits with code 1.

items.title: Operational Notes
items.text:
• Keep backend.consume as an async iterator.
  • Ensure event objects include id, event_name, payload fields.
  • Tune max_concurrency based on downstream capacity.

items.title: Signature Format
items.text:
Fasthooks signs payloads with HMAC-SHA256 when a signing secret is configured.

Header: - X-Fasthooks-Signature: sha256=

items.title: Verification Example
items.text:
import hashlib
import hmac


def verify_signature(payload: bytes, secret: str, header: str) -> bool:
    algorithm, _, received = header.partition("=")
    if algorithm != "sha256" or not received:
        return False
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, received)

items.title: Retry Model
items.text:
Dispatcher behavior: - Retries network failures. - Retries 5xx responses. - Does not retry 4xx responses. - Uses exponential backoff with jitter.

Parameters: - max_retries - backoff_base - backoff_max

items.title: Dead-Letter Hook
items.text:
Use on_failure callback to capture permanently failed deliveries.

Callback signature: - async on_failure(subscription, payload, error)

Common uses: - Write to dead-letter queue. - Emit metrics. - Trigger alerting.

items.title: Hardening Checklist
items.text:
• Use per-environment signing secrets.
  • Set realistic timeout budgets for subscribers.
  • Track delivery failures by event and endpoint.
  • Define subscriber retry ownership clearly.

items.title: Policy Hierarchy
items.text:
• AGENTS.md is canonical and tool-agnostic.
  • CLAUDE.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md are adapters.
  • Python-scoped rules are in .github/instructions/python.instructions.md.

items.title: Repo Rules Agents Must Respect
items.text:
• Keep BackgroundTaskBackend as the only bundled backend.
  • Add non-core transports as external BaseBackend implementations.
  • Preserve backward compatibility unless explicitly requested.

items.title: Recommended Agent Workflow
items.text:
1. Read AGENTS.md before edits.
  2. Apply file-scoped instructions when editing Python under fasthooks.
  3. Keep changes small and verifiable.
  4. Run diagnostics and one smoke check after meaningful edits.

items.title: Built-In Prompt Asset
items.text:
Reusable prompt: - .github/prompts/create-custom-backend.prompt.md

Use this prompt when creating custom Redis/Kafka/SQS backends outside core.

items.title: Drift Prevention
items.text:
• Do not duplicate policy text across many files.
  • Keep adapter files concise and defer to AGENTS.md.
  • Update adapters when AGENTS.md semantics change.

items.title: Current State
items.text:
• Built-in backend: BackgroundTaskBackend.
  • Built-in stores: MemoryStore and SQLStore.
  • Dispatcher supports retries, backoff, HMAC signing, and dead-letter callback.

items.title: Planned Integration Areas
items.text:
• Queue backends via external packages.
  • Telemetry integrations (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Logfire).
  • Additional store adapters (MongoDB, DynamoDB, Redis).

items.title: Suggested Milestones
items.text:
1. Publish a custom backend reference package.
  2. Publish a production dead-letter adapter package.
  3. Add end-to-end examples for queue-backed worker mode.
  4. Add observability docs with concrete exporter setup.

items.title: Compatibility Strategy
items.text:
• Keep core API stable.
  • Add functionality through extension points.
  • Keep optional integrations out of default dependency graph.

items.title: Contribution Direction
items.text:
Good contributions: - Better extension docs and examples. - Hardening for retries/failure callbacks. - Tests around contracts and API behavior.

Avoid by default: - Bundling heavy transport dependencies into core. - Changing backend/store contracts without migration notes.
